rule: The client treats the player as in onboarding when the player's tile falls in one of two onboarding rectangles, and out again inside a third rectangle; the flag is set from the player's tile (Player.setTutorialIsland; the method that calls it was not checked). While the flag is set, fourteen incoming message handlers in Protocol.java skip showing social messages (trade requests, trade lines, quick-chat phrases and others). The server drives onboarding arrows through one HINT_ARROW message: a flags byte (slot in the high bits, target kind in the low bits), a sprite index, then a per-kind target (actor id for kinds 1 and 10, coordinate-style for kinds 2 to 6). The client draws the arrow over the actor and a minimap marker.
keep: Zone-based onboarding flag read from the player's tile, not a player setting
Mute of social noise (trade and quick-chat messages) during onboarding
One hint arrow with a target kind (actor or tile) plus a minimap marker for the same target
Server-sent hint messages: the client never decides what to point at
change: Dim or collapse muted messages instead of hiding them outright, so a rival's message still shows once
Onboarding zone is a row in our zone data, not hard-coded rectangles
Hint arrow message is typed data (target kind, sprite, target), no pixel-offset coupling
look_test: Two runs on Dom's phone, same first 90 seconds: (A) social messages shown; (B) social messages dimmed in the onboarding zone with one hint arrow and a minimap marker. Compare: arrow found within 3 seconds; first fight reads clearly; a rival's message not missed when it matters.
